what_worked: Genuinely thesis-driven narrative with a falsifiable investment screen and honest self-critique on causality.
fix_next: Top-10 share is 49.6% not 50.6%, AI median is $503 not $446, and mean MRR calculation appears off—verify all anchor statistics.
verdict: Exceptional storytelling and design undermined by several verifiable numerical errors.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: Top-10 share stated 50.6% vs reference 49.6%. Slide 4: AI median MRR $446 vs reference median $503. Slide 2: Mean MRR $13,472 vs computed $15,596 from 30-day total.

evidence.insight: Slide 9 cross-tabulation of DR × audience type is original synthesis; slide 10 builds a deployable screen with payback math; slide 4 debunks AI label with hit-rate comparison.
evidence.narrative: Clear myth-busting arc (slides 4-5) builds to signal (6-7), compounds levers (8-9), deploys thesis (10-11), and lands with falsifiable summary and limitations (12). Every slide advances one argument.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets audience (investor), question (what predicts revenue), and scope. Slide 12 explicitly names what would break the thesis. Missing: no discussion of missingness rates (274 category, 288 audience_type).
evidence.accuracy: Top-10 share overstated by 1pp (50.6 vs 49.6). AI median $446 vs $503. Mean MRR $13,472 vs ~$15,596. Slide 6 headline 'explains almost all of it' overstates r=0.48 (~23% variance). Revenue denominators shift between slides without flagging.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark/light palette, strong typographic hierarchy, restrained chart choices (bar, heatmap matrix, stacked bars). Every chart has n-counts and source lines. No decorative graphics. Slide 9 matrix is particularly effective.
evidence.ai_slop: none — deck has a distinctive editorial voice, no filler slides, no generic icons or stock imagery, no inflated consulting language
